# University of Melbourne
The University of Melbourne was established in 1853, funded initially by a government endowment following Victorian gold rush wealth, with classes commencing in 1855. Early faculties included law (1857), engineering (1861), and medicine (1862). Residential colleges affiliated with Christian denominations opened from 1872. Women were first admitted in 1881, with the first female graduate in 1883. Major expansions occurred in the early 20th century, establishing faculties such as dentistry (1911) and agriculture. Post-World War II, student numbers grew rapidly, alongside research prominence.
In 2008, the university introduced the controversial "Melbourne Model," shifting from specialized undergraduate degrees to broader generalist degrees followed by specialized graduate study. Subsequent administrative restructures led to staff cuts and new campus development projects. The university operates the main Parkville campus plus additional metropolitan and regional campuses, including Southbank (arts), Burnley (horticulture), Creswick (forestry), Dookie (agriculture), Shepparton (rural health), Werribee (veterinary), and a forthcoming Fishermans Bend engineering campus. The Parkville campus hosts heritage gothic architecture alongside modern buildings, extensive libraries, galleries, and research centers.
Governed by a 13-member Council with advice from an Academic Board, the university consists of nine faculties—including arts, business and economics, education, engineering, fine arts, law, medicine/dentistry/health sciences, and science. It has a strong research profile with significant expenditure, numerous centers, and a well-developed entrepreneurial ecosystem. Libraries hold over 3.5 million items, supplemented by museums and galleries such as the Ian Potter Museum of Art and Grainger Museum.
The university maintains high national and international rankings (QS 2026: #19 globally, #1 in Australia) and strong employer satisfaction rates. Admission is competitive, with a median ATAR around 94 and 44% international students. Student life includes two main student unions, extensive clubs, sports overseen by Melbourne University Sport, and nine affiliated residential colleges plus university-owned halls of residence. Notable alumni include multiple Australian prime ministers, Nobel laureates such as Elizabeth Blackburn, and figures across arts, science, and public life.
